title: 24-Hour Home Cage Activity Monitoring in Mice
author: Sarah van Veen
materials: Start the activity recording software around noon (12:00). Confirm beam-break counts reset every 30 min. Verify that the 30-min bin intervals are logging correctly. Recording should begin during the light phase so that one full light and one full dark phase are captured in the 24 h window.

steps.title: Place mice in monitoring cages
steps.instruction: Place each mouse individually into a 20 × 30 cm transparent cage positioned between the photo‑beam sensors.

steps.title: Set automated lighting schedule
steps.instruction: Program the lighting to turn OFF at 19:00 (start of dark/active phase) and turn ON again at 07:00 the next morning.

steps.title: Record and export beam‑break data
steps.instruction: Run continuous recording for 24 h, then stop data acquisition and export the beam‑break counts for each animal in 30‑minute bins.

steps.title: Analyze activity by light/dark phase
steps.instruction: For each animal, sum the 30‑min bin counts into light‑phase (07:00–19:00) and dark‑phase (19:00–07:00) totals, then perform a two‑way ANOVA with genotype and phase as factors; healthy controls should show substantially higher activity in the dark phase.

substeps.instruction: Sum 30‑min bin counts into light‑phase (07:00–19:00) and dark‑phase (19:00–07:00) totals for each mouse.
Conduct a two‑way ANOVA with genotype and phase as factors.
Confirm that dark‑phase activity exceeds light‑phase activity in control mice.
